title: Green Bean Casserole with Crispy Onions
summary: Blanched green beans in a cream and browned-mushroom sauce, baked until bubbling and topped with homemade crispy fried onion rings.
equipment: medium frying pan or saucepan for frying

ingredients.item: large onion, sliced into thin rings
fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt, for the cooking water
fine sea salt or table salt
ingredients.note: about ½ tsp, for the sauce

steps.title: Fry the onions
steps.text: Separate the onion rings and toss them in the 40 g flour. Heat the oil in the medium pan to 180 °C and fry the rings in batches for about 3 min until golden and crisp. Drain on kitchen paper and sprinkle with the pinch of salt; the flour coating is what makes them crunchy.

steps.title: Blanch the beans
steps.text: Bring the water and 1 tbsp salt to the boil and cook the beans for about 6 min until crisp-tender. Drain, rinse under cold water and pat dry. Cooling them stops the cooking so they stay green in the oven.

steps.title: Make the sauce
steps.text: Heat the oven to 190 °C (170 °C fan). Melt the butter in the large frying pan over medium-high heat and cook the mushrooms for about 7 min, until browned and their liquid has evaporated. Add the garlic and thyme for 1 min, then stir in the 2 tbsp flour for 1 min. Whisk in the cream, water, soy sauce, salt and pepper and simmer for about 5 min until thickened; the soy sauce adds savoury depth in place of stock.

steps.title: Bake and top
steps.text: Stir in the beans, spread everything in the baking dish and bake for about 15 min until bubbling at the edges. Stir, scatter over the crispy onions and bake 5 min more, until hot through (74 °C). Serve hot.

tips: Brown the mushrooms properly before adding the flour; pale, wet mushrooms give a thin, bland sauce.
Fry the onions in small batches so the oil stays hot and they crisp rather than soak up oil.
Make the sauce and beans up to 4 hours ahead and chill; add 5-10 min to the baking time.
Keep the onions uncovered at room temperature until needed so they stay crisp.
safety: Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Refrigerate leftovers covered up to 3 days. Reheat in a 180 °C (160 °C fan) oven for 15-20 min until piping hot (74 °C); the onions will soften. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
